description: This is a crucial chapter in Logical Reasoning where a sequence of numbers, letters, or symbols is given. Students must identify the underlying pattern to find the next term or the wrong term in the sequence.

sections.title: Number Series
sections.description: Consists of a sequence of numbers following a specific mathematical rule or operation.

results: The difference between consecutive terms is constant (+ or -).
Each term is obtained by multiplying or dividing the previous term by a fixed number.
Terms are based on perfect squares (n^2) or perfect cubes (n^3) of numbers.
Patterns can also be n^2 + 1, n^2 - 1, or n^3 + n.
Applies two or more patterns simultaneously (e.g., multiplication and addition).
Example: x2+1, x2-1 or two alternating series in one sequence.

sections.title: Letter Series
sections.description: Based on the letters of the English alphabet. Remembering the positional values of letters is essential to solve these.

key_concepts.explanation: Positional value from left to right. The EJOTY trick (5, 10, 15, 20, 25) is used to remember this.
Positional value from right to left. To find the backward value of any letter, subtract its forward value from 27 (27 - Forward Value).

results: There is a fixed gap between letters (e.g., +2, +3, or -1).
Groups of 2 or 3 letters are given. The first letter of a group relates to the first letter of the next group, and so on.

sections.title: Alpha-Numeric Series
sections.description: This series features a combination of both letters and numbers.

key_concepts.explanation: Letters follow their own rule and numbers follow a separate rule. Both patterns are independent of each other.
The given number is directly or indirectly based on the positional value of the letter associated with it.

sections.title: Continuous Pattern Series
sections.description: Consists of a series of small letters with some missing elements. The objective is to find a specific repeating sequence of letters.

results: The series is formed by the repetition of identical groups.
Example: a_b_ab -> ab / ab / ab (if the group size is 2).
The sequence of letters changes in a cyclic order.

sections.title: Steps to Solve Series Questions
sections.description: A systematic approach to identify the series pattern with accuracy and speed.

steps.title: Calculate the Difference
steps.detail: Find the difference between consecutive terms. If it increases gradually, it might be an addition series.

steps.title: Check for Rapid Change
steps.detail: If numbers increase or decrease very rapidly, look for multiplication, division, or square/cube patterns.

steps.title: Double Difference
steps.detail: If the first difference shows no clear pattern, calculate the difference of the differences. This solves many difficult questions.

steps.title: Convert Letters to Numbers
steps.detail: In letter series, write the positional values above the letters to visualize the numerical pattern easily.
